details:
Q1: Which branch should the fix go on?
Choices:
A. PR #6650's head branch `ai/issue-6637`. The failure was seen on head `c6edb1d`, so the PR's own change most likely caused it. (RECOMMENDED)
B. The default branch `main`, treating it as a test or poller defect that predates the PR.
C. No new fix. Close this issue as superseded if PR #6650 has since been merged or closed, or its later head passes CI. Its review/autofix loop already gives the editor failing check-runs to fix.
Q2: How should the failing test be identified, since the full shard 1 log is not available to the pipeline?
Choices:
A. Work it out offline. Recompute the test list for `orchestrate-poll (3)` shard 1 using the target branch's `.github/workflows/ci.yml` split (group index 3 of 4, then local shard 1 of `CI_POLL_TEST_SHARDS`=4). Run those tests with `python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py <test_name>` and fix the ones that fail. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Run the whole of `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` on the target branch and fix any failure found. This is slower: about 35 minutes run one after another.
C. Wait until someone posts the `FAIL` line and error text from shard 1 of run 37922343747 (job 113793022264) on this issue, then fix only that test.
Q3: What should happen if the shard 1 tests all pass when reproduced, which would point to a flaky or environment-only failure?
Choices:
A. Close this issue as a no-op with no code change. Post a comment naming the tests that were run and that they passed. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Open a separate follow-up issue to investigate flakiness in the identified tests, and make no code change here.
C. Make the test stricter or more deterministic anyway, based on the most likely cause of flakiness. **Note:** you would need to name the test, so this is incompatible with Q2:C unless that log has been posted.
